changelog: [When to Segment]: fixed the quotative rule — evidence showed splitting between a -다고/-라고 quote and its reporting verb loses the quoted content; the rule now keeps quote+reporting verb together and only permits a split after the reporting verb if a genuinely separate matrix clause follows.

[When to Segment]: added eight concrete permissive rules targeting measured under-segmentation (coordinating -고 with two independently complete clauses; causal -아서/-어서/-니까 with an independent result; conditional -면/-다면 with an independent apodosis; comparative -보다는; chained sequential temporal clauses; leading discourse adverbs like 어쨌든/아무튼; short unambiguous subject pronouns before a long clause; repeated/restated subject before its predicate) — these give free latency gain per the reference splits without harming quality.

[Never Segment]: narrowed the conditional-connective (-면/-다면) prohibition so it only blocks splits when the consequence clause lacks its own subject/verb and borrows the protasis's argument; when the consequence is a genuinely independent clause, splitting is now explicitly allowed, resolving the conflict with the new permissive conditional rule.
